knowledge: DEFEX Engineering is a deliberately small Sydney remedial consulting practice led by Andrew Fisher (BEng(Civil), MIEAust, CPEng, NER; NSW Registered Professional Engineer; NSW Registered Design Practitioner). Tagline: Defects Resolved. The engineer who inspects the building is the engineer who writes the report, prepares the design and superintends the works. Service area: Sydney metro, occasionally Greater NSW. Contact: 0432 261 722, andrew@defex.engineering. Hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00am–5:00pm. Site attendances by arrangement. Services: 1) Defect investigation and diagnostics — A defect report is only as good as its diagnosis. Investigations begin with the symptoms — water ingress, cracking, spalling, movement, failed finishes — and work back to cause through close inspection, targeted opening-up and testing where warranted. Findings are photo-evidenced, keyed to the relevant Australian Standards and NCC provisions, and reported with a clear statement of cause, consequence and recommended action. Reports are written to be read: by owners, committees, insurers and, where necessary, courts. 2) Remedial design and declared designs — Rectification that lasts starts with design, not with a contractor's quote. DEFEX prepares remedial designs and specifications for concrete repair, waterproofing, façade elements and associated structural work. For Class 2 buildings in NSW, regulated designs are prepared and declared under the Design and Building Practitioners Act 2020 by a Registered Design Practitioner, ready for lodgement. 3) Specifications and tender — Remedial work is priced well when it is specified well. DEFEX prepares scopes of works and technical specifications that contractors can price against like for like — then runs the tender: shortlisting, clarifications, tender assessment and a written recommendation. The result is comparable prices, fewer variations, and a contract that starts from a shared understanding of the work. 4) Superintendency and contract administration — Once works proceed, DEFEX administers the contract — typically AS 4000 — as an independent superintendent. Progress claims are assessed against work actually done, variations and extensions of time are valued on their merits, and site inspections keep the works to the declared design through to practical completion and the defects liability period. 5) Expert and litigation-support reporting — Where a defect becomes a dispute, DEFEX prepares reports for use in proceedings — scoped to the questions asked, confined to matters within expertise, and written as a plain statement of cause, consequence and cost of rectification. The same discipline applies whether the report supports a claim, a defence or a negotiated resolution. 6) Façade and waterproofing assessment — Condition assessment before defects become claims: façade elements, balconies, planters, podium decks and roofs — falls-to-drain measured, membranes and terminations inspected, and findings reported against the relevant Australian Standards with a prioritised schedule of recommended works. How engagements run: 01 Contact (describe the building and symptoms), 02 Proposal (written scope and fee in plain terms), 03 Investigation and reporting (photo-evidenced, standards-keyed), 04 Design and delivery (where rectification proceeds, through to completion). The DEFEX platform is the in-house software the practice runs on (site capture with photos tied to defects, project board, timesheets, documents); it is not for sale and has no pricing; clients and builders log in to the projects they are connected to. Enquiries can be sent from the Contact page with photos and documents attached.
